title: You ever make a decision so small…
paragraphs:
You ever make a decision so small…
yet so expensive?

One moment of hunger.
One impulsive choice.
And suddenly a future is gone.
That’s the story of Esau.

He came in from the field exhausted.
Sweat on his skin.
Dust in his beard.
Stomach screaming.
Across the tent sat his brother Jacob, stirring a pot of red stew.
The smell filled the air.
Esau looked at the bowl.
Then Jacob looked at Esau and said something shocking:

“Sell me your birthright.”
— Genesis 25:31
The birthright meant everything.

Inheritance.
Leadership of the family.
The covenant blessing passed down from Abraham.
Generations of promise.
But Esau only saw the stew.

“I’m about to die,” he said dramatically.
“What good is the birthright to me?”
And in one reckless moment…

He traded destiny
for dinner.

“Thus Esau despised his birthright.”
— Genesis 25:34
Brother…
Sister…
This is not just ancient history.

This is every moment we trade eternal things
for temporary cravings.

A relationship God warned you about.
A secret habit you keep feeding.
A compromise that feels good right now.
But costs you later.
The enemy always sells the same lie:
Just this once.
But here’s the Gospel twist.
Where Esau failed…
Jesus did not.
When Jesus Christ was starving in the wilderness, Satan tempted Him with immediate satisfaction.
“Turn these stones into bread.”
But Jesus chose obedience over appetite.
And because He did…
He can redeem every foolish trade we’ve ever made.
Your worst decision is not stronger than His grace.
Not if you bring it to the cross.

Repent.
Return.
Receive mercy.
Because Jesus still restores what we nearly lost.
And sometimes…
He gives back a future we thought we had already traded away.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
